key_insight: A decision-gated, physics-informed surrogate can optimize PV hosting capacity much more reliably than test error alone suggests, even when two surrogates have similar held-out accuracy.
engineering_relevance: The framework speeds stochastic feeder planning while preserving high-fidelity certification, making it useful for practical PV integration studies under uncertainty.
method: Build a stochastic multiobjective optimizer for PV penetration vs. total electrical loss under reliability constraints.
Compare data-only and physics-informed surrogates using decision-relevant screening, then enrich samples near Pareto-critical and constraint-boundary regions.
Verify screened designs with independent high-fidelity certification on 500 scenarios per candidate.
evidence_signal: Although both surrogates had similar held-out errors, operational validity was 44.4% for the data-only model versus 93.4% for the physics-informed model, and 80 screened candidates were all certified with 46 non-dominated designs identified.
watch_item: Results are feeder-specific: a transfer that works on one network can introduce overvoltage and higher losses on another, so independent validation is essential.
paper_title: Decision-Gated Surrogate-Assisted Stochastic Optimization with Independent High-Fidelity Certification for Photovoltaic Hosting-Capacity Planning
